description: India bank/UPI SMS classification + transaction-parse pattern pack. Data-driven port of the Hamza reference (~/CW/Hamza: SmsClassifier.kt, TransactionParser.kt). Used by F-044 (categorization) and F-048 (expenditure parsing). All matching is case-insensitive on the uppercased body/sender unless noted.
source: Hamza (com.example.hamza) — verified against real device inbox Apr–Jun 2026

dltSuffix.note: DLT-registered header suffixes. -P short-circuits to promotional before the transactional content check; -T/-S/-P/-G used as the classifier's final fallback.

classifier.personalRule: sender has no letters, only [0-9 +()-.], digit count in [7,15]
classifier.transactionalRule: transactionalStrong matched, OR (a moneyToken present AND a transactionalVerb present)

parser.creditWordsNote: Bare 'REFUND' intentionally EXCLUDED — it matched pending 'refund initiated/reference'. Only 'REFUNDED' (settled) counts as income.
parser.excludeWordsNote: v2: DELIVERED / OUT FOR DELIVERY / SHIPPED / DISPATCHED - an order/delivery notice that mentions UPI or 'paid' is not a spend (F-048 11.5 'delivery/service all correctly excluded'); bare DELIVERY is deliberately NOT here ('paid for delivery fee' is a real spend). Actual E-Mandate/UPI-Mandate/auto-debit EXECUTIONS carry a 'debited'/'sent' verb (no 'will be') and ARE counted — only the future announcements above are skipped.
parser.nonBankSendersNote: Matched on SENDER only — a merchant named in the body ('spent at ZOMATO') from a bank sender still counts.
parser.rejectPatternsNote: v2: regexes over the UPPERCASED body; a match = NotTransaction. These are credit-card BILL PAYMENT acknowledgements ('Payment of Rs 12,400 received towards your credit card'): the card's purchases are already counted one by one, so counting the bill payment as well double-counts the spend. Bounded repeats only - no unbounded backtracking. The gap between PAYMENT and CARD may not cross ' AT ' or ' TO <merchant>' (so 'Thank you for the payment of Rs 800 AT SHOPX using your Card' and 'payment of Rs 500 TO SWIGGY was received ... Card' are purchases, not bill-payment receipts); ' TO YOUR/THE/CREDIT/CARD' is still allowed. A purchase ON a card ('spent on HDFC Credit Card at AMAZON') has no payment+received wording and is still a debit.
parser.promoWordsNote: Bare 'HTTP'/'WWW.' intentionally EXCLUDED from parser rejects — bank debit alerts carry fraud-report URLs; rejecting them dropped real UPI 'Sent' debits.
parser.balanceNote: v2 (replaces the old fixed 14-char lookbehind, which missed 'AVAILABLE BALANCE IN YOUR ACCOUNT IS INR 5,000' and wrongly dropped a real amount after 'LOW AVL BAL ALERT.'). An amount is a BALANCE, not the transaction, when (a) a balancePrefix word STARTS a word within the balanceContextChars before it, looking back only to the previous sentence boundary (balanceClauseBoundaryRegex) and the previous amount; or (b) the text right after it (<= 64 chars) matches balanceAfterRegex ('Rs 5,000 is your available balance'). The trailing form only fires when the balance word CLOSES the clause (end of text, punctuation, or 'in your account'): when another figure follows it ('debited Rs 500 Avl Bal Rs 2,000') the word labels THAT figure and the 500 is the transaction; 'Rs 500 balance transfer fee' is not a balance either. A balance word only counts when it is a WHOLE word, so 'Dear BALAJI' and 'PVT LIMITED' do not drop the amount. If every amount is a balance the message is Unreadable (a verb with no usable amount, spec D5), never a debit of the balance.

categories.note: F-048 §12 spend-category rules (added for F-056 so desktop and phone share ONE copy). Evaluated in order over UPPERCASE(merchant + ' ' + body); first rule with any trigger as a substring, or any wordTrigger as a WHOLE WORD (not inside a longer run of A-Z letters), wins. v2: the short, ambiguous triggers (CAFE, DTH, ACT, OLA, EMI, LIC, SIP, CRED) moved to wordTriggers - CRED matched inside CREDITED, LIC inside PUBLIC, OLA inside COLA, SIP inside GOSSIP; OLACABS, OLAMONEY, OLAELECTRIC, CAFETERIA, CAFECOFFEEDAY and CREDCLUB are listed as substrings so the real merchants they used to match still do. A credit is always 'Income' (checked before these rules); no match is 'Other'; the pipeline sets 'Transfers' for a detected self-transfer. The UI legend is these names plus Income, Transfers, Other.

algorithm: 1. Reject if sender endsWith '-P' (promotional DLT header).
2. Reject if sender matches any nonBankSenders.
3. Reject if body contains any excludeWords or promoWords.
4. direction: earliest of debitWords (expense) vs creditWords (income); none => NotTransaction.

5. amount: amountRegex.findAll; drop any that is a balance (a whole-word balancePrefix inside the balanceContextChars before it, bounded by the previous sentence boundary / previous amount, or the balanceAfterRegex trailing form); among the rest pick the one NEAREST the direction verb. None => Unreadable.
6. extras: accountRegex tail (last 3–4 digits), merchantRegex (best-effort, nullable).
7. post: markSelfTransfers (same day + same amount debit+credit => isTransfer, excluded from totals); dedupNearDuplicates (same amount+direction within dedupWindowMs).
8. overrides precedence: per-message force-include/exclude > exclude-sender-core > automatic.
